title: Zero-Mem: Zero-Token Memory Operations for LLM Agents
excerpt: I am working on the same thing right now. However, unlike storing conversations in an external retrieval system, I use a local LLM to store the conversation's KV cache and perform retrieval directly on that cache. The method involves running a prefill pass and, after obtaining the attention scores, filtering for the corpus segments that received attention.

 help


I am working on the same thing right now. However, unlike storing conversations in an external retrieval system, I use a local LLM to store the conversation's KV cache and perform retrieval directly on that cache. The method involves running a prefill pass and, after obtaining the attention scores, filtering for the corpus segments that received attention.

This aligns with the "zero tokens" approach described in this paper. :)

I tested it on the LoCoMo used in this paper, and also LongMemEval, both achieved SOTA results.


I was doing something similar where I saved user input/model output in a multi-depth node style storage system (each depth having more precise details) with the focus on the model having accurate user fed information. I was mostly focused on retrieval of accurate / useful information based on user query (injecting the database node as additional, high confidence information)

Once this(Zero-mem) passes it's peer review, I may have to see if my system can handle something similar instead/in addition.

I'm quite excited to see growth in these different ways of eliminating token's.

Long winded aside, @langs, have you published your work on this?


https://github.com/AttemorySystem/attemory/ stars and issues are welcome :)

Using attention for retrieval was inspired by a comment I saw in here long time ago: Prediction and retrieval are two sides of the same coin; to predict better, you must retrieve more accurately.

I'm still working on the improvement of algorithms, my tests shows the performance and accuracy will be improved a lot in the next release.


I am not an expert on LLMs, but what's preventing you from treating the context as 'virtual memory', and using the attention matrix to 'blank out' tokens which have very low weights and will not contribute much to the input? I imagine most tokens are like this, and you can skip computation on 95% of an 1M (or practically infinite) context.


This is actually quite easy to implement at the harness level and the NER can be way more naive because of the typical nature of LLM dialogue (programming, long running tasks etc).


Handling state and memory continuity without heavy token overhead is a massive bottleneck for modern agents. Very interesting approach.


The useful contribution is not zero token cost; it is removing generative rewriting from memory. Preserving original traces avoids a subtle auditability failure: once an LLM compresses an interaction, retrieval is grounded in the summary's omissions rather than the evidence.

I would still want a harder benchmark around mutation and contradiction. If an entity changes attributes across sessions, can the graph and temporal hierarchy preserve both states, surface the conflict, and show which trace justified the answer? The 57.6% time reduction is compelling, but for production agents I would measure unsupported-answer rate and evidence recall under stale, conflicting, and adversarial traces. Encoder compute and index-maintenance cost should also sit beside token cost; otherwise "zero-token" risks being read as "free."

sentences.en: This is actually quite easy to implement at the harness level and the NER can be way more naive because of the typical nature of LLM dialogue (programming, long running tasks etc).

sentences.en: Handling state and memory continuity without heavy token overhead is a massive bottleneck for modern agents.
sentences.zh: 在没有大量令牌开销的情况下处理状态和内存连续性是现代代理的巨大瓶颈。

sentences.en: Very interesting approach.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣的方法。

sentences.en: The useful contribution is not zero token cost; it is removing generative rewriting from memory.
sentences.zh: 有用的贡献不是零代币成本；它正在从记忆中删除生成重写。

sentences.en: Preserving original traces avoids a subtle auditability failure: once an LLM compresses an interaction, retrieval is grounded in the summary's omissions rather than the evidence.I would still want a harder benchmark around mutation and contradiction.
sentences.zh: 保留原始痕迹可以避免微妙的可审核性失败：一旦法学硕士压缩了交互，检索就基于摘要的遗漏而不是证据。我仍然希望围绕变异和矛盾有一个更严格的基准。

sentences.en: If an entity changes attributes across sessions, can the graph and temporal hierarchy preserve both states, surface the conflict, and show which trace justified the answer?
sentences.zh: 如果实体跨会话更改属性，图形和时间层次结构是否可以保留这两种状态、暴露冲突并显示哪个跟踪证明答案合理？

sentences.en: The 57.6% time reduction is compelling, but for production agents I would measure unsupported-answer rate and evidence recall under stale, conflicting, and adversarial traces.

sentences.en: Encoder compute and index-maintenance cost should also sit beside token cost; otherwise "zero-token" risks being read as "free."
sentences.zh: 编码器计算和索引维护成本也应该与代币成本并列；否则“零代币”可能会被解读为“免费”。

blocks.html_en:
The useful contribution is not zero token cost; it is removing generative rewriting from memory. Preserving original traces avoids a subtle auditability failure: once an LLM compresses an interaction, retrieval is grounded in the summary's omissions rather than the evidence.

I would still want a harder benchmark around mutation and contradiction. If an entity changes attributes across sessions, can the graph and temporal hierarchy preserve both states, surface the conflict, and show which trace justified the answer? The 57.6% time reduction is compelling, but for production agents I would measure unsupported-answer rate and evidence recall under stale, conflicting, and adversarial traces. Encoder compute and index-maintenance cost should also sit beside token cost; otherwise "zero-token" risks being read as "free."

sentences.zh: 有用的贡献不是零代币成本；它正在从记忆中删除生成重写。

content_html_zh: 零内存：LLM 代理的零令牌内存操作 (arxiv.org)93 分 by theanonymousone 22 小时前 |隐藏 |过去|最喜欢 | 12 条评论帮助我现在正在做同样的事情。 但是，与在外部检索系统中存储对话不同，我使用本地 LLM 来存储对话的 KV 缓存并直接在该缓存上执行检索。 该方法涉及运行预填充过程，并在获得注意力分数后过滤受到关注的语料库片段。这与本文中描述的“零标记”方法一致。 :)我在本文使用的LoCoMo以及LongMemEval上进行了测试，都取得了SOTA的结果。 我正在做类似的事情，我将用户输入/模型输出保存在多深度节点样式存储系统中（每个深度都有更精确的细节），重点是具有准确的用户反馈信息的模型。 我主要专注于根据用户查询检索准确/有用的信息（将数据库节点作为附加的高置信度信息注入）。一旦这个（零内存）通过同行评审，我可能必须看看我的系统是否可以处理类似的东西/另外。我很高兴看到这些消除令牌的不同方式的增长。长篇大论，@langs，你发表过你在这方面的工作吗？ https://github.com/AttemorySystem/attemory/ 欢迎星星和问题:)使用注意力进行检索的灵感来自我很久以前在这里看到的一条评论：预测和检索是同一枚硬币的两个方面；为了更好地预测，你必须更准确地检索。我仍在致力于算法的改进，我的测试表明在下一个版本中性能和准确性将得到很大的提高。 我不是法学硕士专家，但是是什么阻止你将上下文视为“虚拟记忆”，并使用注意力矩阵来“删除”权重非常低且对输入贡献不大的标记？ 我想大多数令牌都是这样的，您可以跳过 1M（或几乎无限）上下文的 95% 的计算。 这实际上很容易在工具级别实现，并且由于 LLM 对话的典型性质（编程、长时间运行的任务等），NER 可能更加幼稚。 在没有大量令牌开销的情况下处理状态和内存连续性是现代代理的巨大瓶颈。 非常有趣的方法。 有用的贡献不是零代币成本；它正在从记忆中删除生成重写。 保留原始痕迹可以避免微妙的可审核性失败：一旦法学硕士压缩了交互，检索就基于摘要的遗漏而不是证据。我仍然希望围绕变异和矛盾有一个更严格的基准。 如果实体跨会话更改属性，图形和时间层次结构是否可以保留这两种状态、暴露冲突并显示哪个跟踪证明答案合理？ 57.6% 的时间减少是引人注目的，但对于生产代理，我会在陈旧、冲突和对抗性痕迹下测量无支持的答案率和证据回忆。 编码器计算和索引维护成本也应该与代币成本并列；否则“零代币”可能会被解读为“免费”。
